heading: Grokking extends beyond algorithmic data, but training controls depend on the setting
definition: grokking-like delays also appear on non-algorithmic data (images, text, molecules) and can be switched on or off through initialization scale or weight norm (a lazy-to-rich transition).
summary: Independent groups reproduce delays on images, text and molecules; initialization and sustained weight-norm interventions control delays in some small experiments. One-shot rescaling can fail, and a general lazy-to-rich explanation is contested.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy and small image experiments: R2 for behavioral delays, for conditional initialization switches on small image tasks and for conditional sustained weight-norm switches on algorithmic tasks; C for one-shot rescaling or low-norm initialization as a switch in an AdamW modular-addition MLP, which conflicts with quadratic-network small-initialization results; C for an unrestricted lazy-to-rich explanation. Explicit <1B text models: R2 for broadly defined delay analogues, ? for the joint switching/mechanism claim. 1–10B: R0 for local text delays, from one preprint under review; ? for switching/mechanism. 10–100B and >100B: ?; no recorded coverage. Most experimental model sizes are not stated in the count buckets.
suggested_status.reason: The independent reviewed study arXiv:2411.00247 belongs in T1: it exactly replicates the polynomial experiment (arXiv:2411.00247#r1) and adapts the MNIST experiment to binary classification with reduced learning rate and warmup. Its MNIST initialization comparisons support behavioral delays and their removal at standard initialization (arXiv:2411.00247#r7, arXiv:2411.00247#r9, arXiv:2411.00247#r11, arXiv:2411.00247#r13). The lazy-to-rich study supplies MNIST output-scale interventions (arXiv:2310.06110#R7, arXiv:2310.06110#R8). The checks removed arXiv:2607.12735 from V3 support. Sustained weight-norm evidence now rests on the reviewed fixed-norm study, where fixing Transformer weight norm at 30 removes delayed generalization at model dimensions 32, 64 and 128 (arXiv:2505.11411#r4, arXiv:2505.11411#r5, arXiv:2505.11411#r6). It also rests on sustained MLP clamps, with median grokking times of 1,492 steps at rho=0.85 and 27,925 at rho=1.30 (arXiv:2606.13753#r1, arXiv:2606.13753#r13). In the same study, high held norm delays grokking without switching it off within extended budgets, and low norm blocks it at the smallest modulus (arXiv:2606.13753#r18, arXiv:2606.13753#r22). The composite claim has direct challenges. Constant-learning-rate modular-addition Transformer readout-scale trends reverse, and features change from initialization (arXiv:2602.06702#R10, arXiv:2602.06702#R15). The checks relabelled arXiv:2605.27078 as a challenge: it rejects a strict initially fixed-feature phase on algorithmic tasks, where representation learning is already active before onset, and diagnoses the MNIST delay as readout miscalibration over degrading representations (arXiv:2605.27078#r7, arXiv:2605.27078#r10). The same challenges item also groups MNIST kernel movement substantially before grokking (27a0efe7a2e598310a334b01e85aea67c842bc5f#r6), whose pack verdict is limits_scope. The switching component has its own challenge. In an AdamW modular-addition MLP, one-shot global rescaling after memorization leaves grokking time within about 15% of control, and parameter-group rescaling leaves it within about 3% (arXiv:2606.13753#r19, arXiv:2606.13753#r20). That study's text states that low-norm initialization relaxes back to the free timescale (verdict-only, no row). Quadratic-network modular-addition sweeps instead report that small initialization mitigates or eliminates the train–test gap (24541f7b953aa3ca52e53f146aae6ce8b081e3d2#R1, 24541f7b953aa3ca52e53f146aae6ce8b081e3d2#R2; V3.conflicts[2]). The occurrence component has a challenge restricted to MPS HCC gene-expression community C29, where the generalization gain approximately coincides with maximal training accuracy (arXiv:2503.10483#r11). The same study's binary Fashion-MNIST run supports occurrence (arXiv:2503.10483#r1). Their headers mark arXiv:2602.06702, arXiv:2605.27078, arXiv:2606.13753 and arXiv:2503.10483 as preprints; arXiv:2606.13753 reports controls, code and bootstrap uncertainty. OLMoE local asynchronous domain-level text delays support V3's occurrence component (arXiv:2506.21551#r1, arXiv:2506.21551#r2, arXiv:2506.21551#r3, arXiv:2506.21551#r4); neither global synchrony nor a sharp global jump is required. The supplied OLMoE manuscript is a preprint under review, although its pack header and the studies index still say reviewed. Initialization/norm switching remains untested there, which supplies no scope limitation. counts: versions.V3.studies_with_challenges=2 predates the checks. The studies index shows pre-check V3 challenges verdicts only for arXiv:2606.13753 and arXiv:2602.06702, so this count omits the checked challenges from arXiv:2605.27078 and arXiv:2503.10483#r11. versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original=0. The candidates.csv author lists show no author shared with an original for arXiv:2602.06702 or arXiv:2606.13753, and the studies index flags none of the other named studies as same group. versions.V3.studies_by_size contains not stated, <1B and 1–10B, with no larger buckets. C applies to the composite mechanism/general wording, and to one-shot rescaling or low-norm initialization as a switch in the AdamW modular-addition MLP. The behavioral components have independent reproduction.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched optimizer-controlled scale and sustained-norm experiments with direct feature/kernel diagnostics across natural text and molecular data would test the shared-mechanism claim. Replication beyond QM9, seed-robust switching that preserves final generalization, and tests above 10B would change modality, reliability and scale assessments. A matched comparison of one-shot rescaling or low-norm initialization against sustained norm control, run in the AdamW modular-addition MLP, quadratic-network and small-image MLP settings, would show whether the initialization-switch challenge is specific to one setting.

source.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
source.authors: Alethea Power; Yuri Burda; Harrison Edwards; Igor Babuschkin; Vedant Misra

original_result.result: The original paper did not test this claim.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: MNIST grokking depended on training size, weight decay, and learning rate.
Large initialization induced delayed generalization on MNIST and QM9; smaller initialization removed it.
Stronger weight decay replaced modular-division grokking with rapid generalization.
Diffusion models learned distant image combinations abruptly after learning nearer combinations.
ReLU networks generalized on noisy XOR clusters long after fitting training data.
Larger initialization delayed modular-addition grokking, and synthetic classification also showed delayed generalization.
An MLP trained on MNIST images showed delayed generalization.
Narrower teacher-student networks generalized late outside the regime where Gaussian processes approximate network behavior.
Transformers generalized hierarchical language rules long after in-domain validation saturated.
Linear estimators and MLPs reached perfect generalization long after training accuracy saturated.
Non-neural models exhibited initialization-dependent delays on synthetic non-algorithmic tasks.
Scaling network outputs controlled grokking and could eliminate the MNIST delay.
Scaled initialization induced MNIST grokking, with longer delays in deeper networks.
An MNIST MLP's test performance improved late, after training accuracy had stopped improving.
Synthetic regression and MNIST showed delayed generalization; default initialization removed the MNIST delay.
Weight decay switched modular-addition grokking on and off.
Transformers showed delayed generalization on sentiment and instruction tasks with enlarged initialization.
Scaling initial weights induced MNIST grokking that standard initialization avoided.
Deep MNIST networks showed delayed generalization whose pattern changed with weight decay.
Larger initialization prolonged MNIST generalization delays, while standard initialization removed them.
Synthetic odor classification showed abrupt improvement when probing learned features, after training loss converged.
Initializing layers at different scales accelerated modular-arithmetic grokking.
An MNIST MLP initialized with larger weights showed slow, delayed generalization.
Gaussian linear classification exhibited delayed generalization near the separability boundary.
Weight decay and initialization scale controlled modular-addition grokking and its sharpness.
Natural-text pretraining exhibited a grokking-like delay.
MNIST and IMDb showed delayed generalization, while dropout removed the MNIST delay.
BERT's out-of-distribution generalization improved after in-domain performance saturated on MNLI.
Synthetic regression and matrix completion generalized long after training loss approached zero.
Smaller initialization eliminated modular-addition delays associated with late changes in the network's similarity measure (kernel).
Smaller initialization removed modular-addition delays; the network's similarity measure (kernel) changed after overfitting.
Smaller initial weights improved final generalization on parity over input streams and yielded finite-state machines.
Scaling network outputs down could remove delayed generalization on MNIST and EMNIST.
MNIST and Fashion-MNIST grokking persisted with enlarged initialization; stronger decay shortened delays.
Regularization and initialization controlled generalization delays across image and synthetic tasks.
An MNIST MLP generalized late with enlarged initialization, including without weight decay.
Gaussian subclass classification showed late test improvement after training convergence.
Reducing network sensitivity (Jacobian norms) enabled MNIST generalization; holding it high prevented grokking.
A Fashion-MNIST tensor-network classifier improved abruptly after overfitting.
A GPT-2-style model improved late on out-of-distribution text examples built around comparisons.
Methods that modify training updates, Grokfast and EGD, substantially shortened MNIST generalization delays.
MNIST cross-entropy training showed a delayed, incomplete generalization jump as weight decay reduced collapse.
Initialization and regularization controlled delayed generalization in an Ising MLP.
Increasing initialization scale induced grokking on Ising images and modular addition.
OLMoE showed delayed mathematical generalization after web-text pretraining loss converged.
Fixing weight norm removed modular-addition grokking across three network widths.
A ReLU network generalized on XOR clusters long after early overfitting.
Deep and enlarged-initialization MNIST networks showed delayed jumps from chance test accuracy.
Reducing weight scale relative to target output scale removed delayed generalization in an MNIST MLP.
Larger initialization and positive average weight values prolonged modular-addition grokking delays.
Higher learning rate relative to parameter norm enabled feature learning and modular-addition grokking.
MNIST grokking appeared with larger initialization, although the optimizer also changed.
Intermediate weight decay enabled modular-arithmetic generalization, while weak decay left models memorizing.
Pretrained language models showed delayed grammatical generalization that depended on exposure to the grammar.
Smaller circuit initialization shortened an algorithmic generalization delay, but subsequent performance remained fragile.
Quantum networks showed controllable generalization delays on a circles classification task.
An MNIST MLP initialized with larger weights generalized late without weight decay.
Initializations that got stuck delayed Gaussian-data optimization without the usual gap between training and test performance.
Larger network outputs or initial weights induced generalization delays, including on MNIST.
Gaussian feature learning showed initialization-dependent delays; weight decay could keep the model from reaching its target.
Wildfire classification showed late test-performance jumps, though training saturation had not been established.
Weak logit regularization induced delayed generalization in Gaussian linear classification.
Regression grokking depended on weight decay and, for ridge regression, initialization scale.
Sustained weight-norm changes strongly altered grokking times across algorithmic tasks.
MNIST grokking disappeared under standard training, with initialization and dataset size changing together.
Clamping weight norm postponed modular-addition generalization beyond the observation window.
Estimates of hypothetical alternative outcomes improved smoothly after predictive performance saturated, without a sharp generalization jump.
IMDb and cross-entropy MNIST showed weaker grokking under unusual or confounded settings.
Normalizing classifier weights and features did not invariably remove late generalization.
CelebA showed partial delays; timing of generalization to new combinations depended on data properties.
The XOR grokking guarantee required specific assumptions and a bounded training horizon.
Modular-addition grokking persisted without weight decay, with a slower and less sharp transition.
Teacher-student generalization delays depended on noise and vanished near the limit where fixed kernels approximate networks.
Very shallow and very deep transformers rarely generalized hierarchical rules after a delay.
Linear-model delays depended on data ratio and thresholds without a lazy-to-rich transition.
Smaller initialization reduced delay growth but did not remove dimension-dependent grokking.
Teacher-student delays appeared in threshold accuracy while losses tracked throughout training.
Changing how synthetic data were sampled switched grokking on or off without changing initialization.
Standard image, speech, and language training showed no sudden memorization-to-generalization transition.
Language grokking was smoother and imperfect, with Yelp delays disappearing at larger dataset fractions.
Image and text models with standard initialization gained adversarial robustness late, after clean accuracy converged.
Shallow MLPs showed weaker grokking with more training data, disappearing at 7000 points.
Replacing cross-entropy with hinge loss removed delayed test improvement.
Grokking depended on data separability and weakened with small noise under gradient descent.
MNIST grokking persisted even as the weight norm increased.
Image grokking followed early changes in network kernels (similarity measures); otherwise-identical EMNIST runs varied across seeds.
Tested image and text models showed no generalization delay despite initialization scaling.
Large initialization and small weight decay produced abrupt error drops to suboptimal linear solutions.
Training-data composition switched grokking on or off under a fixed training regime.
Gene-expression classification gains varied across groups, including a group with no generalization delay.
Reasoning delays depended on data augmentation and task structure; composition tasks showed no late out-of-distribution jump.
A toy model plateaued only with both a suitable data-distribution shape and suitable initialization.
Scaling MNIST weights by 100 caused collapse that blocked delayed generalization.
Text benchmarks showed local, asynchronous generalization delays without a global jump.
Modular-addition grokking persisted even after the initialization scale was tuned.
MNIST delays depended on training settings and disappeared with test-time batch statistics.
Zero-initializing the top layer shortened modular-addition grokking delays without eliminating them.
Increasing the positive initialization offset shortened delays or impaired generalization, depending on the offset's size.
Tensor-network classifiers showed no clear generalization delay on Fashion MNIST and overfit hyperspectral data.
With high effective learning rates, generalization required attention inputs to decrease in magnitude.
With default initialization, sampling distribution and dataset size determined whether regression showed delayed generalization.
The grammar benchmark Determiner–Noun Agreement 2 showed no delayed generalization.
A plain MLP memorized noisy XOR clusters without generalizing within 5000 steps.
Delays from scaling the output layer appeared only when learning rate and weight decay also changed.
In quantum circuits, grokking depended on depth; norm penalties did not have a consistent effect.
Increasing initialization and output scales reduced late-stage gains measured against training error.
Checkpoint-induced delays lacked prior training saturation and disappeared with fresh random initialization.
MNIST delays depended on optimizer and appeared narrowly with cross-entropy.
Across weight-decay sweeps, accuracy in the worst-performing group showed no delayed transition on CelebA or Waterbirds.
Linear-model recovery required boundary-focused testing; standard synthetic and MNIST tests showed no delay.
Data properties set plateau duration, while initialization changed its length without eliminating it.
Wildfire classification showed uneven class learning without a single sharp generalization jump.
With ReLU features, larger initialization did not significantly prolong grokking; Fourier-feature grokking required careful tuning.
Holding weight norms constant changed delays, depending on the divisor in modular arithmetic and LayerNorm.
MNIST delays reflected a poorly calibrated output layer; algorithmic tasks showed internal representation changes before grokking.
Increasing transformer output-layer scale accelerated generalization, while features changed continuously from the start of training.
Rescaling weights once barely changed grokking time; effects of initially small weight norms faded during training.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A matched demonstration that the same lazy-to-rich mechanism explains initialization, output-scale and sustained Euclidean-norm interventions across natural images, text and molecular tasks.
untested.basis: Pack untested-parts lines separate occurrence, switching and mechanistic characterization. QM9 has initialization controls but no accompanying lazy-to-rich diagnostic; text observations and negative partial-scaling tests do not supply a successful matched mechanism test. counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size and weight_edit.by_size contain only not stated; family counts cannot establish this joint test.

untested.what: Molecular-delay replication beyond Omnigrok's QM9 polarizability setup, with quantified baseline delay and matched switching controls.
untested.basis: Omnigrok supplies the molecular on/off evidence; Grokfast's untested-parts line says QM9 baseline delays are not quantified. Neither part supplies another molecular-delay test. counts: versions.V3.studies_by_family has no molecule-specific category, so this gap rests on the pack evidence rather than family classification.

untested.what: V3 occurrence or switching tests at model sizes of 10–100B or above 100B.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size and versions.V3.coverage_by_operation contain no 10–100B or >100B bucket. The displayed larger text example is 7B OLMoE; its findings concern local delays rather than initialization/norm switching.

untested.what: Successful initialization/norm switching with direct regime diagnostics in the explicitly size-bucketed text models.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size includes <1B and 1–10B, but versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size, training.by_size and weight_edit.by_size contain only not stated. The corresponding text observations leave initialization/norm switching untested.

untested.what: Extension of the two-layer ReLU XOR-cluster guarantee beyond its dimension, signal-to-noise, initialization and step-size assumptions or bounded generalization horizon, including a controlled high-signal comparison.
untested.basis: arXiv:2310.02541#R2 and arXiv:2310.02541#R4, corrected by the checks: Theorem 3.1 assumes A1–A6 and bounds the generalization horizon by √n. The larger-signal explanation concerns cited prior work; this study reports no controlled high-signal comparison. counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation does not distinguish these theorem assumptions or horizons, so this gap rests on the cited evidence.

wording_issues.phrase: Set by the training regime, not the data
wording_issues.issue: Sampling distribution, subclass coverage, separability and signal strength change whether delays appear under fixed training recipes. In CelebA conditional image generation, underrepresented Male attributes converge later than Female attributes and require continued training beyond initial training-set convergence. This frequency-linked delay does not establish an on/off switch. The exclusive wording does not fit the observed dependence on data properties.

wording_issues.phrase: can be switched on or off
wording_issues.issue: High-norm censoring does not establish permanent absence; extended training can recover grokking. In sustained norm-clamp experiments on algorithmic tasks, eventual grokking at high held norm remains an observed norm-dependent timing effect. Departure from an exponential timing extrapolation does not imply weakening of that delay. Other off conditions prevent generalization instead of producing rapid generalization.

wording_issues.phrase: through initialization scale or weight norm
wording_issues.issue: The evidence also uses output/logit scaling, relative layer initialization, effective learning rate, Jacobian norms and input/target scaling. These are distinct controls. Some initialization comparisons change optimizer, decay or data size simultaneously. In the representation-readout MNIST comparison, the changed recipe eliminates grokking and its diagnostic signatures, but initialization scale, sample count and training duration change together, so the isolated initialization effect cannot be determined.

A delayed accuracy curve or scale sensitivity does not establish an initially lazy phase. The modular-addition Transformer study reports significant feature change throughout training, which the authors interpret as evidence against an initial lazy phase. Representation diagnostics also reject a strict initially lazy phase on algorithmic tasks and diagnose MNIST delay as readout miscalibration over degrading representations. EMNIST diagnostics show early kernel movement. Linear-model delays can arise without nonlinear feature emergence.

The phrase covers held-out accuracy after training fit, OOD accuracy after ID validation saturation, copying after loss stabilization, exposure-conditioned threshold lags and asynchronous local text gains. Their operational definitions differ.

The cited measures do not all establish delayed generalization after training saturation. Wildfire training saturation is unshown. Prepared-checkpoint deep-linear delays lack canonical train/test dissociation in dense data; sparse-data escape lowers training and test error together. Streaming-parity initialization/data sweeps measure final validation accuracy and automaton structure, not delay timing. The cited optimizer grids classify final states; temporal measurements are reported separately. The convergence sweeps and final-state grids therefore cannot establish temporal on/off switching.

wording_issues.phrase: can be switched on or off through initialization scale or weight norm
wording_issues.issue: Switching is conditional on architecture and intervention: multiplying initialization by eight only in feedforward and linear layers fails to induce delays in text Transformers on SST-2, TREC-6 and AG-news. This comparison does not test whole-network initialization scaling. Initialization has little timing effect in random ReLU features, small explicit QNN L2 leaves timing ratios unchanged, and visual shortcut decay sweeps show no transition.

method_sensitivity.factor: Isolated initialization versus jointly changed recipes
method_sensitivity.what: Frequency-study MNIST comparisons change initialization, optimizer and learning rate together; with default initialization, training and test accuracy rise simultaneously and grokking is absent. Omnigrok's IMDb comparator changes initialization and decay. Representation-readout MNIST comparisons change initialization, training-set size and training duration: grokking and diagnostic signatures disappear completely under the comparator, but attribution specifically to initialization is undetermined. That study attributes the MNIST delay to readout miscalibration over degrading representations, challenging the strict lazy-to-rich interpretation.

method_sensitivity.factor: Optimizer, scale compensation and effective learning rate
method_sensitivity.what: On modular addition under AdamW, readout-scale trends reverse between inverse-square-scaled and constant learning rates: at learning rate 0.001, higher scale generalizes faster while delayed generalization remains observed. On MNIST, LM compresses delay across the scale sweep with lower final test accuracy; the individual alpha=1 delay is undetermined. EGD changes MNIST threshold-attainment time. In the modular-addition protocol with weight projection, layer normalization and scale decay, rewarming to 0.01 activates feature learning and grokking after prolonged low-rate training, whereas 0.001 fails. Warmup to 0.01 followed by cosine decay rapidly produces perfect test accuracy retained after one million optimizer steps.

method_sensitivity.factor: Duration and target of norm interventions
method_sensitivity.what: In algorithmic-task experiments, sustained norm clamps alter timing strongly where one-shot rescaling has little effect. Low norms can block generalization; high-norm absence depends on budget. Saturation relative to an exponential timing extrapolation leaves the norm-dependent delay observed. On modular division, classifier/feature normalization preserves grokking at temperature 0.25 despite stable training. In the large-initialization MNIST setup, Jacobian-norm minimization permits generalization while holding that norm high prevents it. These interventions control different quantities and produce different outcomes.

method_sensitivity.factor: Data amount, composition and evaluation distribution
method_sensitivity.what: Uniform versus nonuniform sampling, subclass coverage, concept frequency and boundary-concentrated evaluation create, remove or change delays under otherwise matching recipes. In the attribute-generation comparison, Female curves converge faster than underrepresented Male curves; generating underrepresented attributes requires continued training beyond initial training-set convergence.

method_sensitivity.factor: Loss, logit regularization and numerical stability
method_sensitivity.what: Large-scale cross-entropy can stop learning through Softmax Collapse without decay. The synthetic odor-classification MLP shows delayed probe accuracy under cross-entropy; with hinge loss, probe loss and margin stop improving when training loss does. The accuracy transition establishes delayed generalization but does not itself establish a gradual mechanism. Weak quadratic logit regularization enables Gaussian-classification delays absent without it. Softmax temperature and dropout alter Ising delays.

Depth changes CFG and MNIST delay occurrence. Under weight projection with LayerNorm, scale decay restores generalization; without scale decay, high effective learning rate fails to generalize. BN evaluation statistics remove an apparent deep-MNIST delay. Negative CNN, ViT and text-Transformer initialization tests use selected-layer scaling: CNN scaling affects fully connected layers, ViT scaling affects feedforward layers and the linear head, and the cited text-Transformer test multiplies initialization by eight only in feedforward and linear layers.

On modular arithmetic, dividing positional and token embeddings by alpha, multiplying logits by tau and dividing learning rate by tau² changes grokking time, with fastest grokking in an unbalanced rich setting; total parameter norm is not controlled. In the four-layer tanh MNIST MLP, lowering initialization, increasing target scale, decreasing input scale or decreasing output scale removes delay. The adapted ReLU MNIST 3-vs-5 replication, using reduced learning rate and warmup, reports longer delays at larger initialization. At alpha=1 without sigmoid, training and test behavior are almost identical and grokking is absent; a generalizing solution is found in about 10^2 rather than 10^5 steps.

method_sensitivity.factor: Seeds, training budget and successful-switch criteria
method_sensitivity.what: EMNIST induction varies across seeds. Stiefel-routing small initialization is a single-seed pilot with a fragile later trajectory, establishing initialization sensitivity rather than a reliable on/off switch. Convergence-only streaming-parity sweeps measure final validation accuracy and representation structure; final-state optimizer grids classify outcomes after fixed update budgets. These endpoint measurements leave temporal delay switches undetermined for V3 and provide measurement coverage rather than support for switching.

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation granularity, thresholds and loss trajectories
method_sensitivity.what: OLMoE domain curves show stable lagged gains while paired groups show local asynchronous delays; both support delayed generalization on text. The cited paired group has an annotated delay of 120k pretraining steps, from Pretrain@5k to Test@125k. Global synchrony and a sharp global jump are not V3 requirements. LLaMA-style exposure-conditioned threshold lags vary by grammatical phenomenon and run. Threshold accuracy can show teacher-student grokking while MSE tracks; STARNet PEHE improves after R² saturates.

Smaller decay prolongs ridge-regression delays. Fixed-large-initialization MNIST can grok without decay and later collapse, while decay prolongs retention. Prepared deep-linear checkpoints produce optimization delays absent from fresh random initialization, but dense-data runs lack canonical train/test dissociation. In sparse-data runs, both errors fall at escape. This is an incomplete grokking analogue; checkpoint preparation does not test an initialization-scale or weight-norm switch. QNN decay can shorten successful-run timing while lowering success.

status_amendment.public_note: The status now weighs every challenge found in checking (further evidence against the lazy-to-rich explanation, a modular-addition study where one-off weight rescaling or small initialization did not remove the delay, and one gene-expression community that showed no delay), and it notes that the 7B text-model evidence comes from a preprint under review. The suggested level is unchanged: it stays challenged for the claim as a whole, while the delays themselves and some initialization and weight-norm switches have independent reproductions.
